notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: I read the complete held EO 12513 (50 FR 18629, May 1, 1985): declares a national emergency over Nicaragua, prohibits imports and exports and transactions, bars Nicaraguan air carriers and vessels, and delegates IEEPA powers to the Secretary of the Treasury; no own term. I read the complete held EO 12707 (55 FR 9707, Mar. 14, 1990, 'Termination of Emergency With Respect to Nicaragua'): 'I hereby revoke Executive Order No. 12513 and terminate the national emergency declared in that order', 'This order shall take effect immediately.' Its savings paragraph (NEA sec. 202) preserves only actions taken, pending proceedings, acts committed before, and matured rights or penalties; it does not keep any prohibition or delegation of EO 12513 operating, so there is no partial scope left. Earlier endings: none found; the four annual Notices (Apr. 22, 1986; Apr. 21, 1987; Apr. 25, 1988; Apr. 21, 1989) continue the emergency and precede the revocation. D6 (later events): the history's later events are those Notices (before the end) and the EO 12707 revocation; I searched the held corpus for any order naming EO 12513 and found only EO 12707, so nothing amends, revives or extends it after 1990 (the later Nicaragua sanctions order, if any, rests on separate authority and does not name it). The OFR 'Revoked by: EO 12707' note and the revocation candidate event agree with the held acting text, but the basis is the text. Provisional NO hypothesis only.
